req.title: Support all HTTP verbs on /status/<code>
req.statement: The system shall accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE on /status/<code>.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /status/<code> must accept GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, OPTIONS, and TRACE. The source shows the route is registered for GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, TRACE (not HEAD or OPTIONS explicitly, but Flask handles HEAD automatically for GET routes). Tests cover: (1) positive EP for each supported verb returning the exact requested status code, (2) negative path for invalid/non-numeric codes returning 400, (3) boundary values at status code edges (100, 200, 299, 300, 400, 500, 599), (4) decision table for weighted/comma-separated codes, (5) exact status code pass-through to kill constant-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_all_verbs_accept_status_200
actions: Send GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, TRACE to /status/200
trace: R-HTTPBIN-017 — DT: all registered HTTP verbs must return the requested status code
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_verbs_accept_status_200():
    methods = [
        client.get, client.post, client.put,
        client.patch, client.delete, client.trace
    ]
    for method in methods:
        r = method('/status/200')
        assert r.status_code == 200, f'{method} did not return 200, got {r.status_code}'

test_all_verbs_accept_status_200()

tests.name: test_options_not_registered_returns_405
preconditions: OPTIONS is not in the route's methods list
expected: Response status code is 200 (Flask auto-handles OPTIONS) OR 405 if not supported — assert it is not a 5xx error
trace: R-HTTPBIN-017 — NEG: OPTIONS not explicitly in route methods; Flask may auto-respond or return 405
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_options_not_registered_returns_405():
    r = client.options('/status/200')
    # Flask auto-handles OPTIONS returning 200 with Allow header
    # The route does NOT list OPTIONS, so Flask returns its own 200 with Allow
    # Either way it must NOT be a 5xx error
    assert r.status_code != 500
    assert r.status_code != 501
    assert r.status_code != 502
    # Flask typically returns 200 for OPTIONS with Allow header
    assert r.status_code in (200, 405)

test_options_not_registered_returns_405()

tests.name: test_boundary_status_200_vs_199
actions: Send GET /status/199 and GET /status/200 and compare
trace: R-HTTPBIN-017 — BVA: boundary ±1 around 200, catches off-by-one mutations in status_code()
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_boundary_status_200_vs_199():
    r199 = client.get('/status/199')
    assert r199.status_code == 199
    r200 = client.get('/status/200')
    assert r200.status_code == 200
    assert r199.status_code != r200.status_code

test_boundary_status_200_vs_199()
